renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: ani_dot_plot
  title: Detected genomes per sample
  description: |-
    Each dot is a reference genome that sylph detected in a sample: its colour is the adjusted containment ANI and its size is the taxonomic abundance as a fraction. It answers which genomes are present in which samples and how close each match is.
    How to read: large dark dots are abundant genomes with a close match. A small dot with a lower ANI is a divergent relative of the reference, so the sample holds a different strain or species than the database. A genome present in every sample is part of the shared community.
    Source: https://sylph-docs.github.io/Output-format/
  kind: dot_plot
  roles:
    cluster: sample
    gene: genome
    mean_expression: adjusted_ani
    frac_expressing: abundance_frac

- component: figure
  title: ANI against abundance
  description: |-
    Each point is a genome detected in a sample: its taxonomic abundance on the horizontal axis and its adjusted ANI on the vertical axis, coloured by sample and sized by effective coverage. It answers whether the abundant genomes are also the confident, close matches.
    How to read: points at the upper right are abundant and near identical to the reference. A point with low abundance and low ANI is a weak or divergent detection to treat with care. Large points have more coverage behind their ANI.
    Lines and annotations: The dashed line is the median adjusted ANI of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of sylph.
    Note: sylph reports a coverage-adjusted ANI only below 3x coverage and otherwise the naive ANI, so very deep genomes are not adjusted.
    Source: https://sylph-docs.github.io/Output-format/
  visu_type: scatter
  dict_kwargs:
    x: taxonomic_abundance
    y: adjusted_ani
    color: sample
    size: eff_cov
    labels:
      taxonomic_abundance: Taxonomic abundance (%)
      adjusted_ani: Adjusted ANI (%)
      sample: Sample
      eff_cov: Effective coverage
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: adjusted_ani
    label: Median adjusted ANI

- component: card
  title: Adjusted ANI
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median adjusted containment ANI of the detected genomes, and the box shows the spread. It answers how close the sample genomes are to the reference genomes.
    How to read: values near 100 percent mean the sample holds the reference strain. A lower median means divergent relatives of the references, so the database may lack the exact genomes.
    Note: containment ANI slightly overestimates the true ANI.
    Source: https://sylph-docs.github.io/Output-format/
  column: adjusted_ani
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Detected genomes
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct reference genomes detected, and the strip counts detections, a genome found in two samples counting twice. It answers how rich the profiled communities are.
    How to read: many detections of few genomes means a shared community across samples. A detection count close to the genome count means each sample has its own genomes.
    Source: https://sylph-docs.github.io/Output-format/
  column: genome
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: genomes, with detections counted

- component: card
  title: Effective coverage
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median effective coverage of the detected genomes, a k-mer based estimate of the sequencing depth, with the lowest and highest values. It answers how deeply each detected genome is covered.
    How to read: a low coverage means a thin detection whose ANI is less certain. High coverage detections support the ANI and the abundance.
    Note: the cited sylph page gives only a minimum of more than 0.01 to 0.05x coverage to detect a bacterial genome and states no coverage cut-off, so none is drawn here.
    Source: https://sylph-docs.github.io/sylph-can-cannot/
  column: eff_cov
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: grid
  caption: median, with the lowest and highest genome

- component: table
  title: Detected genomes table
  description: |-
    Each row is a reference genome detected in a sample, with its taxonomic and sequence abundance, adjusted and naive ANI, effective and median coverage, and containment. It answers the exact values behind every tile.
    How to read: sort by adjusted ANI to find the weakest matches, or filter by sample to list what it contains.
    Source: https://sylph-docs.github.io/Output-format/

- component: card
  title: Genome containment
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median share of a reference genome's k-mers that were found in the sample, and the box shows the spread. It answers how much of each detected genome is actually present in the reads.
    How to read: a high share means most of the genome is contained in the sample. A low share with a high ANI is a low coverage detection, since few k-mers were sampled.
    Source: https://sylph-docs.github.io/Output-format/
  column: containment_frac
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: advanced_viz
  id: stacked_taxonomy
  title: Taxonomic composition per sample
  description: |-
    Each bar is a sample and each segment a taxon at the chosen rank, sized by its taxonomic abundance as a percentage, with the smaller taxa merged into Other. It answers which taxa make up each community and how the samples differ.
    How to read: similar bars mean similar communities, and a taxon that dominates one sample only marks a difference worth following up. Switch the rank to move between phylum and species, and use the controls to sort the samples or hide taxa.
    Note: sylph abundance is coverage-normalised, like MetaPhlAn, and is not a read count share.
    Source: https://sylph-docs.github.io/Output-format/
  kind: stacked_bar
  config:
    top_n: 8
    value_title: Taxonomic abundance (%)
  roles:
    sample_id: sample_id
    taxon: taxon
    rank: rank
    abundance: abundance

- component: card
  title: Distinct taxa
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct named taxa detected, and the bars rank the taxonomic ranks by how many taxa each holds. It answers how rich the profile is and at which rank.
    How to read: a rank with many taxa is where the communities are most diverse. The count of rows beside it counts a taxon once per sample.
  column: taxon
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: rank
  top_n_count: 4
  filter_expr: col('taxon') != ''
  caption: distinct taxa, by rank
  headline: true

- component: table
  title: Taxonomic profile table
  description: |-
    Each row is a taxon in a sample, with its full lineage, its rank and its taxonomic abundance. It answers the exact abundance behind every segment of the composition.
    How to read: filter by rank and sort by abundance to list the dominant taxa of a sample.
    Source: https://sylph-docs.github.io/Output-format/
